reviews.summary: Authentication and onboarding review found two medium abuse-control gaps plus a low-risk build-time dependency chain.

findings.title: Password brute-force protection absent
findings.description: Password verification is performed without a shared persistent attempt limit.
findings.recommendation: Add persistent rate limiting by IP and normalized account identifier, progressive backoff, Retry-After, and security-event logging.

findings.title: Unrestricted privileged tenant onboarding
findings.description: Public onboarding creates an active organisation and privileged roles without abuse controls; duplicate responses disclose registered emails.
findings.recommendation: Rate limit onboarding, require a verified email or invitation, return generic duplicate-account responses, and add abuse monitoring.

findings.title: Vulnerable build-time dependency chains
findings.description: npm audit reported five high-rated advisories, currently entering through development tooling rather than a confirmed runtime path.
evidence: Chains reviewed through ESLint, Prisma development tooling, Jest or ts-jest
findings.recommendation: Refresh lockfiles and overrides, run test/build verification, and retain effective severity as Low unless a runtime path is established.

reviews.summary: Admin authentication can silently fall back to a shared password, and development dependency advisories remain.

findings.title: Admin MFA can silently downgrade to shared password
findings.description: Password-only bootstrap authentication is enabled whenever no AdminUser records exist.
findings.recommendation: Disable fallback in production after initial provisioning, fail closed if accounts disappear, and alert on fallback activation.

findings.title: Vulnerable build-time dependency chains
findings.description: npm audit reported three high-rated advisories, currently entering through development tooling rather than a confirmed runtime path.
evidence: Chains reviewed through ESLint, Prisma development tooling, Jest or ts-jest
findings.recommendation: Refresh lockfiles and overrides, run test/build verification, and retain effective severity as Low unless a runtime path is established.

reviews.summary: The credential callback bypasses the preparation endpoint throttle; one low-risk development dependency advisory remains.

findings.title: Login throttle bypass
findings.description: Only the preparation endpoint is rate limited; credentials are independently verified without throttling and can be submitted directly to the NextAuth callback.
findings.recommendation: Enforce throttling inside authorize() or at middleware/proxy level covering every credential submission.

findings.title: Vulnerable build-time dependency chains
findings.description: npm audit reported one high-rated advisory, currently entering through development tooling rather than a confirmed runtime path.
evidence: Chains reviewed through ESLint, Prisma development tooling, Jest or ts-jest
findings.recommendation: Refresh lockfiles and overrides, run test/build verification, and retain effective severity as Low unless a runtime path is established.

reviews.summary: Live service, off-host backup, runner and TLS checks passed; authenticated monitoring and restore evidence were not tested.

findings.title: Authenticated synthetic and restore evidence absent
findings.description: The service was active with zero restarts, its database was present in the successful encrypted off-host backup, and TLS had 85 days remaining; no authenticated synthetic, alert target, or restore drill was evidenced.
evidence: Nightly encrypted off-host DB backup succeeded; runner active; TLS 85d
findings.recommendation: Add a DB-backed health synthetic and quarterly restore proof, and document RPO/RTO.

reviews.summary: App and marketing services were healthy with off-host backup and runner coverage; end-to-end and restore proof remain gaps.

findings.title: Frontend-only checks do not prove DB-backed operation
findings.description: Both hosts returned 200 and both units had zero restarts; the database was backed up off-host, but a DB-backed synthetic and restore proof were not evidenced.
evidence: Off-host DB backup succeeded; runner active; TLS 70d
findings.recommendation: Monitor both frontends and a DB-backed path, then record quarterly restore proof.

reviews.summary: App and marketing services, backup, and runner were healthy; expiry, DB-backed synthetic, and restore coverage remain incomplete.

findings.title: Expiry and DB-backed resilience checks are incomplete
findings.description: Both endpoints returned 200 and units had zero restarts, while certificate validity was 42–43 days; no DB-backed synthetic or restore drill was evidenced.
evidence: Off-host DB backup succeeded; runner active; TLS 42/43d
findings.recommendation: Add certificate-expiry alerting, a DB-backed synthetic, and a recorded restore drill.

reviews.summary: Production and staging were live and the historical 502 was not current; environment-specific monitoring remains incomplete.

findings.title: Production and staging need separate restart monitoring
findings.description: Production returned 200 to login with zero restarts and staging was active; the database backup and runner were healthy.
evidence: Production service active; 0 restarts since 2026-08-05; staging active
Off-host DB backup succeeded; runner active; TLS 85d
findings.recommendation: Monitor production and staging separately, alert on restart loops, and document the prior credential-failure fix.

reviews.summary: The panel and runner were live, but self-monitoring, state-backup classification, and near-term certificate renewal need explicit controls.

findings.title: No external watchdog for Mission Control
findings.description: The panel was healthy behind nginx, but monitoring from the same system leaves a self-monitoring blind spot.
findings.recommendation: Add an external watchdog that alerts independently of Mission Control.

findings.title: State backup classification and certificate renewal need confirmation
findings.description: Mission Control was not visible in the DB backup manifest and its certificate had 30 days remaining.
evidence: No Mission Control datastore in observed DB backup manifest
findings.recommendation: Confirm state is disposable or externally persisted, otherwise add it to backup coverage; verify renewal before 2026-09-07.

reviews.summary: Application, public, support, backup, and scheduled services were live; job outcome age and recovery proof remain gaps.

findings.title: Timer activity does not prove job outcome or recovery
findings.description: App, site, support, and remote-support services were healthy and the core encrypted backup succeeded, but job result age and restore behavior were not tested.
evidence: App/login, public and support hosts returned 200
App/web active with 0 restarts; remote-support Up 7d
Report/Entra timers running; core off-host DB backup succeeded; TLS 82d
findings.recommendation: Monitor job result and age, perform a restore drill, and add dependency checks.

reviews.summary: Edge policy and encrypted backup were verified, but the protected backend was not exercised end to end.

findings.title: CRM8 needs an allowlisted end-to-end synthetic
findings.description: A 403 from the non-allowlisted source proves edge policy only, not backend or dependency health.
evidence: Edge returned expected 403 from non-allowlisted source
findings.recommendation: Add an allowlisted synthetic that exercises the backend and monitor the backend-host and Tailscale recovery path.

reviews.summary: Serving, backup and deployment runner were healthy; restart history, renewal, and restore evidence need follow-up.

findings.title: Restart history and 30-day certificate require follow-up
findings.description: PM2 was online with four lifetime restarts and two days uptime; the certificate had 30 days remaining.
evidence: Off-host DB backup succeeded; runner active; TLS expires 2026-09-07
findings.recommendation: Investigate and document restarts, alert on restart rate, verify renewal before 2026-09-07, and perform a restore drill.

reviews.summary: Serving, process, backup, and runner checks passed; DB-backed monitoring and recovery proof remain incomplete.

findings.title: DB-backed synthetic and restore evidence absent
findings.description: PM2 was stable and the encrypted backup succeeded, but the operational review did not evidence a DB-backed synthetic or restore drill.
evidence: Off-host DB backup succeeded; runner active; TLS 40d
findings.recommendation: Add a DB-backed synthetic, certificate-expiry alert, and quarterly restore proof.

reviews.summary: Serving and process state were healthy, but ABEA has the portfolio's highest confirmed backup gap.

findings.title: No scheduled encrypted off-host ABEA database backup
findings.description: Only an ad-hoc 2026-07-17 SQL backup was found; ABEA was absent from the nightly off-host manifest and active runner set.
evidence: Ad-hoc 2026-07-17 SQL backup only; absent from nightly off-host manifest and runner set
findings.recommendation: Establish scheduled encrypted off-host backup with retention and restore testing; verify deployment workflow and add certificate alerting.

reviews.summary: Serving and local backup were healthy, but observed backup archives were not off-host.

findings.title: CounselDesk backups remain local-only
findings.description: The daily local backup completed, but observed archives were absent from the encrypted off-host manifest.
evidence: Observed archives absent from encrypted off-host manifest
findings.recommendation: Encrypt and copy backups off-host, monitor freshness and size, and perform a restore test.

reviews.summary: The static site was healthy, but deployment remains manual and lacks auditable smoke and rollback controls.

findings.title: EffectX deployment is manual and unaudited
findings.description: The site was served as a static nginx export and deployment documentation described a manual pull/build path.
evidence: TLS 82d; deploy documented as manual pull/build
findings.recommendation: Add an auditable GitHub deployment with smoke verification and rollback, and confirm the repository is authoritative.

reviews.summary: The service was live, but persistence, backup, deployment provenance, and health coverage were not inventoried.

findings.title: Persistence and recovery coverage are not inventoried
findings.description: The endpoint and PM2 process were healthy, but the project was absent from the nightly DB manifest and runner list.
evidence: Absent from nightly DB manifest and active runner list
findings.recommendation: Inventory persistence and repository ownership, record deploy provenance, add project health monitoring, and back up any stateful data.

reviews.summary: The process was live, but persistence, backup, deploy provenance, and project health evidence were incomplete.

findings.title: Persistence and recovery coverage are not inventoried
findings.description: PM2 was healthy, but OrgCharts was absent from the nightly DB manifest and runner list.
evidence: Absent from nightly DB manifest and active runner list
findings.recommendation: Inventory persistence, add health and deploy provenance, and establish backup coverage where stateful.

reviews.summary: Hearth Command was live, but its local-only repository and persistence/recovery coverage need inventory.

findings.title: Local-only service lacks persistence and recovery inventory
findings.description: The endpoint and PM2 process were healthy, but no remote, runner, or nightly DB-manifest evidence was found.
evidence: Absent from nightly DB manifest and active runner list; local-only repository
findings.recommendation: Establish repository ownership, inventory persistence, record deploy provenance, add health monitoring, and back up any stateful data.

reviews.summary: Its PM2 process was live, but the public endpoint, owner, persistence, backup and deploy path were not mapped.

findings.title: Public endpoint and operational ownership are unmapped
findings.description: PM2 was online, but the project was absent from nightly backup and runner evidence and its public endpoint was not mapped.
evidence: Absent from nightly DB manifest and active runner list
Public endpoint and operational owner not mapped
findings.recommendation: Map the public endpoint and owner, inventory persistence, record deploy provenance, and add backup where stateful.

reviews.summary: Serving, scheduled collection and encrypted SQLite backup were present; job freshness and restore behavior were not monitored.

findings.title: Collector freshness and failure are not structured signals
findings.description: The daily collector was flock-protected and SQLite was backed up, but collection exit/freshness and stale-price alerting were not evidenced.
evidence: SQLite included in nightly encrypted backup; TLS 37d
findings.recommendation: Alert on collector exit, collection freshness, and stale prices; add structured job monitoring and an SQLite restore test.

reviews.summary: The site and certificate were healthy, but statefulness, ownership, deployment and backup coverage were unknown.

findings.title: Statefulness and deployment ownership are unknown
findings.description: The site was reachable, but no dedicated backup or runner evidence was observed and static versus stateful operation was not established.
evidence: No dedicated backup or active-runner evidence observed
findings.recommendation: Map owner and repository, classify the service as static or stateful, and add deploy provenance and monitoring.

reviews.summary: The website was serving normally, but its analytics systemd unit was failed.

findings.title: jeffa-analytics.service is failed
findings.description: The public site remained healthy while its analytics unit was in a failed state.
findings.recommendation: Repair the analytics unit or explicitly retire it, and assign alert ownership.

reviews.summary: The website was serving normally, but its analytics unit was failed and deploy provenance was not established.

findings.title: spacecadet-analytics.service is failed
findings.description: The public site remained healthy while its analytics unit was in a failed state.
findings.recommendation: Repair or explicitly retire the analytics unit and establish auditable deploy provenance.
